the deluding creative power that produces the dual world; here said to be of Viṣṇu's own nature (v.56)
nescience, the root of the rope-snake error; the technical opposite of jñāna
the Self / the supreme Self, here identified with Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa; the core ontological subject, not merely 'soul'
the absolute, the non-dual ground of being, apprehended as reflected in the intellect (v.19, 24, 57)
the conscious principle/person, contrasted with prakṛti; the term the disciple explicitly asks about (v.7)
primal material nature, the source of the manifest world; the Sāṃkhya substrate
the three constituent qualities of prakṛti; the inert guṇa-apparatus is the locus of all action (v.11, 37)
limiting adjunct that makes the all-pervading Self appear conditioned; basis of the crystal/water/pot analogies
superimposition / illusory error (the snake imagined on a rope); the epistemic mechanism of bondage
action and its ripening fruit; burnt by the fire of knowledge like a roasted seed (v.39)
liberating knowledge of the truth, whose fire destroys the seed of karma and birth
the field-knower, the embodied conscious self; v.47 'many kṣetrajñas spring from one'
the fourth, transcending the three states of waking, dream, and deep sleep (v.31)
absolute aloneness/isolation; the liberated one (kevalin), the work's name for the goal (v.70, 81, 83)
